To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
market-seeking and client-following strategies are positively associated with new venture formation while resource-seeking strategies are negatively associated with new venture choice.

(1) market-seeking and resource- seeking strategies are associated with the choice of new venture formation, (2) the client- following strategy is not associated with the choice for new venture formation, and (3) the choice for new ventures is positively associated with market-seeking and resource -seeking strategies, but not with client- following strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of country-specific strategies on new venture formation for firms entering Central East Europe.
the impact of country-specific strategies on new venture formation in the context of internationalization in Central and East European (CEE) countries.
the impact of country-specific strategy on the choice of new venture formation for firms investing in Central and East European markets.

there is a relationship between country-specific strategies and the decision to start up new venture.
the market-seeking and resource seeking strategies are the most important determinants of new venture formation.
the choice of the country-specific strategy influences the choice of the venture strategy.

the country specific strategy of an MNE is a key factor for the choice between a greenfield venture and an acquisition.

the influence of country-specific strategies on new venture formation is dependent on the type of strategy pursued by the firm.
